name: Healthcare Advisory Committee
authority: Section 222 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 217a); Federal Advisory Committee Act
reportsTo: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz. CMS staffs the committee and the Administrator appoints its members.
focusAreas: Chronic disease prevention, outcomes accountability, real-time data, vulnerable populations, Medicare Advantage sustainability
thesis: The committee is built to protect the incumbent healthcare industrial complex: large hospital systems, Medicare Advantage insurers, value-based care platforms, and the health IT infrastructure that serves them. The branding promises disruption. The roster guarantees continuity.
notAtTable: Rural hospital administrators outside a system
Patient advocacy organizations unaffiliated with industry
Medical school debt and physician workforce experts
Physicians who have testified against hospital consolidation
Academic researchers on hospital market concentration
State attorney general staff investigating health system pricing

sources.label: CMS press release naming the members, March 26, 2026

charter: Signed August 19, 2025; amended March 16, 2026 to allow up to 20 members. Two-year terms for members and the chair.

nextMeeting.text: Virtual public meeting. The committee votes on 15 working-group recommendations, including site-neutral pricing, Medicare Advantage and VA payment overlap, broker reform and Food is Medicine in Medicaid.

meetings.label: Orientation (closed) and Meeting 1 (public)
meetings.text: Members sworn in; bylaws adopted 15 to 0; six working groups formed. Kennedy and Oz attended the closed session. Robbins absent, sworn in the next day.

meetings.label: Meeting 2 (virtual)
meetings.text: Agenda: each working group presents its vision and initial ideas. No summary, transcript or coverage located as of November 6, 2026.

meetings.label: Meeting 3 (virtual)
meetings.text: Vote on 15 proposed recommendations: collaborative care, Food is Medicine in Medicaid, site-neutral pricing, real-time claims integrity, Medicare Advantage and VA overlap ($22 billion), agent and broker reform, plan transparency, credentialing through the National Provider Directory, Medicaid data modernization.

workProducts: Bylaws and Meeting 1 materials only. No report or recommendation has been sent to HHS or CMS as of November 6, 2026.

scrutiny.text: AACOM: no osteopathic physicians were appointed.
Public Citizen: financial conflicts are widespread and no patient or consumer representative sits on the committee.
Senators Merkley and Wyden wrote to Kennedy and Oz: most members are executives or investors who stand to benefit; they question FACA balance. No reply found.
Public Citizen urged HHS and CMS to disband or reconstitute the committee.
